editorial.tono: Clear, informed, respectful, calm and independent. Write in natural English with an accessible international news style. Be factual and concise while providing enough context for readers who are not familiar with the Vatican or Catholic terminology. Distinguish clearly between verified facts, official statements, historical interpretation and editorial analysis. Avoid sensationalism, clickbait, speculation, conspiracy theories, partisan political language and excessive religious jargon. Use a respectful tone when discussing the Pope, the Catholic Church and religious beliefs. Never imply that LeoPope is affiliated with the Holy See or the Vatican.

ilustraciones.estilo: Refined editorial photography and documentary-style illustrations about Pope Leo XIV, the Vatican and the Catholic Church. Vertical 4:5 format, natural light, realistic details, subdued European news-magazine aesthetic, deep burgundy, ivory, charcoal and muted gold accents. Calm, respectful, intelligent and informative mood. Use authentic-looking Vatican architecture, public ceremonies, books, documents, artwork and symbolic details. Keep the main subject in the upper-right third and leave clean negative space for layout. When the headline names the Pope or another public church figure acting in their public role, they may appear, rendered as a clearly drawn or painted editorial illustration rather than a photorealistic image that could be mistaken for a real photograph of the event, shown at middle distance, in profile, from behind or in a wide shot, recognisable by vestments and setting, with no facial close-ups and no attempt at facial likeness. Never private individuals, minors, victims, or anyone accused or under investigation. No text, logos, watermarks, official Vatican emblems, papal keys, tiaras or flags. Avoid sensationalism, fictional events and images that make the account appear officially affiliated with the Vatican.

banco.texto: I prefer a Church which is bruised, hurting and dirty because it has been out on the streets, rather than a Church which is unhealthy from being confined and from clinging to its own security.
Humanity still has the ability to work together in building our common home.
No one is saved alone; we can only be saved together.
Being Christian is not the result of an ethical choice or a lofty idea, but the encounter with an event, a person, which gives life a new horizon and a decisive direction.
Do not be afraid. Open wide the doors for Christ.
